text:
ConocoPhillips rose 1.5% today after crude oil prices jumped sharply—Brent crude gained more than 4% on news that the U.S. is deploying a third aircraft carrier strike group to the Middle East, escalating tensions in a region that handles a large share of global oil shipments. As a major oil producer, ConocoPhillips benefits directly when oil prices rise, since higher crude prices mean higher revenue per barrel sold.

The move fits a broader pattern this week: the stock fell steadily from Tuesday through Thursday as oil remained under pressure, but rebounded today on geopolitical risk. The tension around Middle Eastern shipping lanes and U.S. military involvement creates genuine uncertainty about oil supply, which typically lifts prices and energy stocks even amid broader economic concerns.
